patch.value: Count of Participants That Achieve Pathologic Complete Response (PCR)
PCR is defined as the absence of any residual invasive cancer on hematoxylin and eosin (H&E) evaluation of the resected breast specimen and all sampled ipsilateral lymph nodes.

eventGroups.description:
Patients receive paclitaxel IV and carboplatin IV on day 1 (course 1 only) or day 2 (courses 2-12). Treatment repeats every 7 days for 12 courses in the absence of disease progression or unacceptable toxicity. Beginning 21 days after the last course, patients receive doxorubicin hydrochloride IV and cyclophosphamide IV on day 1. Treatment repeats every 21 days for 4 courses in the absence of disease progression or unacceptable toxicity.

outcomeMeasures.title: Count of Participants That Achieve Pathologic Complete Response (PCR)

outcomeMeasures.description:
The proportion of subjects with each category of overall clinical response will be summarized by presence of baseline measureable disease (i.e., complete response [CR], partial response [PR], stable disease [SD], progressive disease [PD], unable to evaluate [UE], neurogenerative disease [ND]).
Beta will be used as priors for combination regimens in calculating the posterior distribution of the PCR for each respective treatment group.
Among subjects with measurable disease, a 95% credible region will be calculated for the odds ratio for each treatment combination relative to each other.
outcomeMeasures.title: Overall Clinical Response

outcomeMeasures.description: Analyzed using Kaplan-Meier methods, stratified by study group, and the log rank test will be completed.
